podcast.title: Involvement in Copyright Case
podcast.body: Albert Hammond Sr. was one of the litigants in the copyright infringement trial against Radiohead concerning their song "Creep," which was found to be similar to his 1972 song "The Air That I Breathe" by The Hollies. Consequently, he now receives 25% of the writing credit for Radiohead's "Creep." "One of the litigants in this trial was Albert Hammond, the father of Albert Hammond Jr. of the Strokes."

podcast.title: Prolific Songwriter
podcast.body: Albert Hammond Sr. is a successful songwriter who wrote numerous songs for a wide array of prominent artists. His credits include songs for Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters. He also received a writing credit on Radiohead's song "Creep" due to its melodic resemblance to "The Air That I Breathe," a song he wrote for The Hollies in the 1970s, as determined by a court case. "He wrote this song. Dad also wrote songs for Celine Dion, where we at the Franklin Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, the Carpenter, and a ton of others."

xref.title: Albert Hammond Jr.'s Background and Role
xref.body: Albert Hammond Jr. is the son of Albert Hammond Sr., a successful songwriter who wrote songs for artists like Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Willie Nelson, Chicago, and The Carpenters, and had a writing credit on Radiohead's "Creep." In the early days of The Strokes, Albert was the band's business guy, booking gigs and pitching record companies under the pseudonym "Paul Spencer" (from his fake ID). He collected rejection letters by posting them on a wall. Crucially, he had a credit card funded by his father, which paid for essential band expenses like guitar strings, cables, drumsticks, and rehearsal PA. "Albert was the business guy of the band in the early days. He was the guy who booked gigs and pitch record companies, usually under the pseudonym Paul Spencer, which was the name he used on his old fake ID."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Albert Hammond Jr.'s Drug Problem
xref.body: During the period leading up to the "Angles" album, Albert Hammond Jr. developed a severe drug problem stemming from a breakup. He used heroin, cocaine, and ketamine, described as "a mess," and required time in rehab to address his addiction. "Another thing, Albert Hammond Jr. had developed a nasty drug problem from a breakup and required time in rehab."

xref.title: Albert Hammond Jr.'s Fashion Line
xref.body: Albert Hammond Jr. developed a significant interest in fashion. He launched his own line of men's suits and ties, with a particular enjoyment for designing ties. "He even has his own line of men's suits and ties. He really likes designing ties."

xref.title: Band Formation and Early Members
xref.body: Julian Casablancas and Nikolai Fraiture met at age six while attending a prestigious French school in New York City. Julian met Albert Hammond Jr. at the Institute Le Rose, a highly expensive private boarding school in Switzerland. By 1997, Julian and Nick Valensi were at Dwight School, where they met Fabrizio Moretti and started a band. Albert moved from Switzerland to New York for film school, became Julian's roommate, and joined the band, with Nikolai joining shortly after as the bassist. "By 1997, Julian and Nick were attending a college prep school called the Dwight School. Again, not cheap."

xref.title: Diverse Musical Career
xref.body: Sean Lennon, the son of John Lennon and Yoko Ono, has had a varied musical career. He has been a member of multiple bands, composed scores for films, produced material for other artists, and released several solo albums. He has also collaborated with prominent figures such as Albert Hammond Jr. of The Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey. "Sean Lennon is the son of John and Yoko. He's been in a bunch of different bands, scored some films, produced material for other people, recorded a couple of albums on his own, and collaborated on records with people like Albert Hammond Jr. of the Strokes, The Flaming Lips, Lady Gaga, and Lana Del Rey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Struggles and Financial Support
xref.body: In the late 90s, the New York rock scene was considered dead, with few venues beyond private parties in Brooklyn warehouses. The Strokes worked through these challenges with Albert Hammond Jr.'s father's credit card and part-time jobs. Julian Casablancas was a bartender at Max's Kansas City, Nikolai Fraiture worked at a video store, Fabrizio Moretti made smoothies, and Albert Hammond Jr. worked at Kim's video. "Along with Albert's dad's credit card, they also had part-time jobs."

xref.title: New York Origins (Upper West Side)
xref.body: The Strokes originated from three "preppy kids" on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, Julian Casablancus, Nick Valenci, and Fabio Moretti, all sons of affluent parents. Julian later met Albert Hammond Jr. at a private boarding school in Switzerland. "They start with three preppy kids on the upper west side of Manhattan, sons of rich parents."

xref.title: Trust Fund Band – Most Members from Wealthy Families, Casablancas Money Bankrolled Early Career
xref.body: Almost every member of The Strokes came from wealthy backgrounds. Singer Julian Casablancas is the son of John Casablancas, head of the Elite Model Agency, home to Cindy Crawford, Linda Evangelista, Claudia Schiffer, Tyra Banks, Cameron Diaz, and Heidi Klum. Julian attended a private school in Switzerland where he met Albert Hammond Jr., the son of 1970s singer-songwriter Albert Hammond ("It Never Rains in Southern California"). Drummer Fabrizio Moretti's parents sent him to the Dwight School, a Manhattan prep school, where he met Julian and guitarist Nick Valensi — the only relatively modest-background member. Bassist Nikolai Fraiture grew up in a two-bedroom apartment with five relatives but still attended a prestigious bilingual school on the Upper West Side. The Casablancas family money funded the band's early gear and operations. "No wonder so many other bands were jealous."
